newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The privatisation committee decided at its last meeting that the state would sell 10 percent of Suez Cement from the stake owned by public-sector bodies which did not contribute to the GDR issue last year, including some of the state-dominated cement companies. The sale will be to the public through the stock exchange.

- Kamal Ghoneim, the chairman of the state's Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills, said that milling companies have cut the price at which they sell flour of 72 percent extraction but that this was a result of the fall in world prices of wheat. He said this would not reduce the profit margins of the companies.

- Hafez Ghandour of National Bank of Egypt said institutions showed great interest in the bond offer by Arab African International Bank and that demand exceeded the 300 million pounds ($88 million) which the bank wants to raise, even before the offer opens to applications.

- Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals made net unaudited pre-tax profits of 8.46 million pounds in the first six months of the financial year 1996/7, 160 percent up on the same period of last year.
- Heliopolis Housing and Development made unaudited profits of 38.9 million pounds in the six months up to the end of December, against 31 million in the same period of the previous year.

- Kima/Egyptian Chemical Industries KIMA.CA made net unaudited pre-tax profits of about 12.8 million pounds in the first six months of the financial year 1996/7, 37.5 percent up on 9.325 million pounds in the same period of the previous year.
- Upper Egypt Flour Mills net profits of 32.8 million pounds in the six months up to the end of December, against 21.6 million in the same period of 1995.
- Hafez Ghandour of National Bank of Egypt said an offer of shares in Egypt Cement was more than nine times oversubscribed. The offer closed last Tuesday.
